## Why we should talk

To the CRPPA community: I propose a conversation on behalf of our FKRP patient community.

Our diseases have a documented biological connection: CRPPA makes CDP-ribitol, a substance that FKRP needs. [E02] This gives us a reason to talk, not proof that the same treatment would work for both communities.

## What already exists that we could share

CureLGMD2i serves the FKRP community, while the LGMD Awareness Foundation serves both our communities. [G1] [G2]

The Global FKRP Registry exists, but its status is unknown in the supplied information. [A1] “Biomarker Development in LGMD2i” is completed, and “Long-Term Development of Muscular Dystrophy Outcome Assessments” is listed as recruiting. [A2] [A3]

We could start by sharing these public study links and exploring whether any approaches are relevant to your community; that relevance is untested.

## What is different between our diseases

The biological connection involves different roles: CRPPA makes the substance FKRP needs. [E02]

Ribitol is in clinical development for FKRP; a CDP-ribitol prodrug rescued a CRPPA-deficient mouse, but CRPPA evidence is preclinical only. [E04] Any treatment bridge between our communities is inferred, not established. [E04]

Even within FKRP, the same gene can cause mild limb-girdle disease or severe congenital muscular dystrophy, so shared biology should not erase disease differences. [E06]

## What we propose this month

Let us arrange an introductory community meeting, exchange the public resource links above, and draft a short shared information sheet separating observed evidence from inferred links.

We propose collaboration on information—not treatment recommendations or promises of results.
